notes: The double כָּהֵם is the hardest allocation here: the first כְּ takes how many soever, the second takes the supplied copula may be as the clause's prepositional predicate (rules 20, 49), and the second pronoun is unrepresented under rule 22. The competing reading gives may be to the first pronoun and marks both members of the second pair unrepresented.
מֵאָה פְעָמִים fuses as hundredfold; both lexemes stand in the one English word, so the head is the governing morpheme standing first (rules 23, 30).
The demonstrative pronoun takes the phrase's single determiner this, leaving both articles unrepresented (rule 41).
